To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the interventional nature of IR systems has not been sufficiently understood, (ii) recommendation is not only an interventional process but it also transports the learned pattern to the intervention domain.
(1) recommendation is not only an intervention, but also a domain transportation, and (2) we propose a principled transportation constrained risk minimization objective to optimize recommendation.

(1) the interventional nature of recommender systems is often overlooked, which leads to biased evaluation and invalid learning; (2) we propose a novel framework that rephrases optimizing recommendation as finding the best transportation between the observed domain (data) and target domain (distribution); (3) we design a transportation-constraint risk-minimization objective to solve this minimax game and develop an efficient and effective algorithm to solve the problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) what is the consequence of violating overlapping assumption, and what can be done to mitigate it; (ii) how to formulate and optimize recommendation as domain transportation; and (iii) what can we learn from this new perspective.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel perspective on recommendation, which not only helps to explain why the current recommendation systems fail, but also leads to a principled framework to optimize recommendation.
we provide a new perspective of understanding recommendation and a novel approach to optimizing it.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of IR systems, the intervention of recommendation should be carefully designed and interpreted, and the evaluation should be conducted with caution to avoid misleading conclusions.
recommendation is not just about learning, but about transporting the learned knowledge to its target domain.

, in order to optimize recommendation, we should consider both the learning and intervention effects, and the consequence of intervention should be taken seriously when designing the objective and algorithm.
